In '90, I joined the Marines, then became a geologist.  Knowing I wanted a 'better' boot than issued ones, I originally bought a pair of Danners, wore through college.  After the side of my Danners blew out, I wanted something even better; this coincided with an article in Backpacker magazine about 25 years ago that had a Limmer Lightweight on the cover. I drove to the nearest shop that carried them, bought my pair of Limmer Lightweights, and they'd severed me well for 20 years. Finally had a chance to pass through New Hampshire several years ago, stopped by the Limmer shop.  Dropped that pair off, as they needed to be resoled.   But while there, after examining those boots and my feet, they walked over and handed me another pair to try, a black custom pair.  As great as my Lightweights were, these were even better.   Limmer shipped my other pair back to me once they were done; it's really great knowing that I have two pair of the best boots in the world, and they'll easily last all the rest of my time able to get around in.  I'm tickled that you've covered them.

I have a pair of Bavarian style hiking boots from one of the old Austrian bootmaking families as well. Specifically the Steinkogler Bergwachts. These are their lightest and cheapest hiking model, similar in a way to the Limmer Lights. Still, they can take a beating. I've been using them on construction among brick and rubble and they're fairing great. Of course they make heavier models with outer leathers going well over 3 mm in thickness. 

And somewhat similar to Limmer, the reason I managed to get a pair is thanks to the lifetime dedication of a single hiking enthusiast who wanted to bring back old style welted, tough and repairable boots. He not only sells them, but repairs and resoles them and makes stuff like creams for them. He actually started making his own (very heavy, very tough) boots as well, so I hope he's lucky with that as well.

And actually, seeing those Bavarian style closed lacing shoes on someone else, I might pay the guy a visit. He has them with a slicker city style sole and I've been debating with myself whether I'd like them for summer or not. Now I might know...

Love this!  I got my custom Limmers about a month ago after getting fitted last November.  I was on the waiting list for a year and half I think.  I had wanted to get a pair of Limmers for over a decade but just couldn't get to the shop from SoCal very easily. It's been a ton of anticipation. But I stopped in New Hampshire on my way back from Europe and got fitted.  It was so much fun to see the shop, I got a whole tour!  I bought a pair of Ultralights while I was at the a shop to help tide me over for the 4 months or so it was going to take to get my custom boots.  I had a ton of fun breaking in the stock boots but I will say it wasn't easy... and those are the light boots.  I hadn't broken in a boot like that in 30 years and I had a few blisters and sore feeting at first.  I'm having a totally different experience with the the custom boots.  They are stiff and tight for sure but no blisters and no sore feet.  They fit so perfectly I haven't had any issues and they begin to be more comfortable each week.  Obviously, I still have many miles to go until both sets of boots are fully broken in but out of the gate the customs are a whole different experience.  The Ultralights are comfortable now, and no more blisters, but I still have small issue on my left foot wear my pinky toe is suffering a bit while the boot stretches to fit better.  I don't have that problem with the customs at all.  Overall, I love Limmers and really enjoy this video and the sister video @CarlMurawski did.  It's great to see a company with this much history and such a great Limmer family feel, even if the family has a lot of adopted members at this point.

Re: Limmer Boots—I’ve been on the waitlist for just over a year. When I visited for the first time, I was surprised to find that Limmer was only 15 minutes from my family home of 30 years… they really don’t do advertising.

Adam gave me a tour of the shop, walking me through every step of the bootmaking process as if I were the only customer to have walked through the door in years. One of the stock guys had already impressed me with the level of detail with which they assessed every inch of my foot—from the vamp and quarters to the shaft—before bringing me over to Adam’s station.

Those stock boots already felt more comfortable than anything I had worn before, and given my particular anatomy, they were confident that a custom pair would far exceed even those. I was sold. I can’t wait for my number to come up.
